# ripgrep defaults that keep secret stores out of ordinary searches.
#
# The guard allows plain `rg` because these exclusions make it safe; without
# them, `rg TOKEN .` prints matching lines from .env files. Point ripgrep at
# this file (or merge the globs into your own config):
#
#   export RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.config/ripgrep/config"
#
# Format: one argument per line, no shell quoting. Lines starting with # are
# comments. Command-line flags override what is set here, which is why the
# guard denies --no-ignore, --no-config, -uu and positive globs that re-include
# protected names.

# Searching dot-directories is common; never descend into .git/.
--hidden
--glob=!.git/

# No positive template re-include: it turns the search into a whitelist. Use
# Read or explicit-file rg for .env.example/.sample/.template outside stores.
--iglob=!.env
--iglob=!.envrc
--iglob=!.env.*
--iglob=!*.env
--iglob=!*.secret
--iglob=!.secrets/
--iglob=!.secrets.env
--iglob=!.netrc
--iglob=!.git-credentials

# Tool credential files the guard also protects. SSH public keys are excluded
# with the private ones; read them directly when needed.
--iglob=!.npmrc
--iglob=!.pypirc
--iglob=!**/.aws/credentials
--iglob=!**/.aws/config
--iglob=!**/.docker/config.json
--iglob=!**/gh/hosts.yml
--iglob=!**/.ssh/id_*

# Cloud, registry and developer credential files. The home-only Yarn rule in

	filemode = true

# ripgrep defaults that keep secret stores out of ordinary searches.
#
# The guard allows plain `rg` because these exclusions make it safe; without
# them, `rg TOKEN .` prints matching lines from .env files. Point ripgrep at
# this file (or merge the globs into your own config):
#
#   export RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.config/ripgrep/config"
#
# Format: one argument per line, no shell quoting. Lines starting with # are
# comments. Command-line flags override what is set here, which is why the
# guard denies --no-ignore, --no-config, -uu and positive globs that re-include
# protected names.

# Searching dot-directories is common; never descend into .git/.
--hidden
--glob=!.git/

# No positive template re-include: it turns the search into a whitelist. Use
# Read or explicit-file rg for .env.example/.sample/.template outside stores.
--iglob=!.env
--iglob=!.envrc
--iglob=!.env.*
--iglob=!*.env
--iglob=!*.secret
--iglob=!.secrets/
--iglob=!.secrets.env
--iglob=!.netrc
--iglob=!.git-credentials

# Tool credential files the guard also protects. SSH public keys are excluded
# with the private ones; read them directly when needed.
--iglob=!.npmrc
--iglob=!.pypirc
--iglob=!**/.aws/credentials
--iglob=!**/.aws/config
--iglob=!**/.docker/config.json
--iglob=!**/gh/hosts.yml
--iglob=!**/.ssh/id_*

# Cloud, registry and developer credential files. The home-only Yarn rule in
# the guard is conservatively excluded here at every level. Project .yarnrc.yml
# remains readable directly, but can contain npmAuthToken values.
--iglob=!**/.kube/config
--iglob=!application_default_credentials.json
--iglob=!**/gcloud/credentials.db
--iglob=!**/gcloud/access_tokens.db
--iglob=!**/gcloud/legacy_credentials/
--iglob=!.vault-token
--iglob=!**/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json
--iglob=!**/.cargo/credentials.toml
--iglob=!**/.cargo/credentials
--iglob=!.pgpass
--iglob=!.yarnrc.yml

--iglob=!.secrets/

# ripgrep defaults that keep secret stores out of ordinary searches.
#
# The guard allows plain `rg` because these exclusions make it safe; without
# them, `rg TOKEN .` prints matching lines from .env files. Point ripgrep at
# this file (or merge the globs into your own config):
#
#   export RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.config/ripgrep/config"
#
# Format: one argument per line, no shell quoting. Lines starting with # are
# comments. Command-line flags override what is set here, which is why the
# guard denies --no-ignore, --no-config, -uu and positive globs that re-include
# protected names.

# Searching dot-directories is common; never descend into .git/.
--hidden
--glob=!.git/

# No positive template re-include: it turns the search into a whitelist. Use
# Read or explicit-file rg for .env.example/.sample/.template outside stores.
--iglob=!.env
--iglob=!.envrc
--iglob=!.env.*
--iglob=!*.env
--iglob=!*.secret
--iglob=!.secrets/
--iglob=!.secrets.env
--iglob=!.netrc
--iglob=!.git-credentials

# Tool credential files the guard also protects. SSH public keys are excluded
# with the private ones; read them directly when needed.
--iglob=!.npmrc
--iglob=!.pypirc
--iglob=!**/.aws/credentials
--iglob=!**/.aws/config
--iglob=!**/.docker/config.json
--iglob=!**/gh/hosts.yml
--iglob=!**/.ssh/id_*

# Cloud, registry and developer credential files. The home-only Yarn rule in
# the guard is conservatively excluded here at every level. Project .yarnrc.yml
# remains readable directly, but can contain npmAuthToken values.
--iglob=!**/.kube/config
--iglob=!application_default_credentials.json
--iglob=!**/gcloud/credentials.db
--iglob=!**/gcloud/access_tokens.db
--iglob=!**/gcloud/legacy_credentials/
--iglob=!.vault-token
--iglob=!**/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json
--iglob=!**/.cargo/credentials.toml
--iglob=!**/.cargo/credentials
--iglob=!.pgpass
--iglob=!.yarnrc.yml

--iglob=!.yarnrc.yml

# ripgrep defaults that keep secret stores out of ordinary searches.
#
# The guard allows plain `rg` because these exclusions make it safe; without
# them, `rg TOKEN .` prints matching lines from .env files. Point ripgrep at
# this file (or merge the globs into your own config):
#
#   export RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/.config/ripgrep/config"
#
# Format: one argument per line, no shell quoting. Lines starting with # are
# comments. Command-line flags override what is set here, which is why the
# guard denies --no-ignore, --no-config, -uu and positive globs that re-include
# protected names.

# Searching dot-directories is common; never descend into .git/.
--hidden
--glob=!.git/

# No positive template re-include: it turns the search into a whitelist. Use
# Read or explicit-file rg for .env.example/.sample/.template outside stores.
--iglob=!.env
--iglob=!.envrc
--iglob=!.env.*
--iglob=!*.env
--iglob=!*.secret
--iglob=!.secrets/
--iglob=!.secrets.env
--iglob=!.netrc
--iglob=!.git-credentials

# Tool credential files the guard also protects. SSH public keys are excluded
# with the private ones; read them directly when needed.
--iglob=!.npmrc
--iglob=!.pypirc
--iglob=!**/.aws/credentials
--iglob=!**/.aws/config
--iglob=!**/.docker/config.json
--iglob=!**/gh/hosts.yml
--iglob=!**/.ssh/id_*

# Cloud, registry and developer credential files. The home-only Yarn rule in
# the guard is conservatively excluded here at every level. Project .yarnrc.yml
# remains readable directly, but can contain npmAuthToken values.

--iglob=!.vault-token
--iglob=!**/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json
--iglob=!**/.cargo/credentials.toml
--iglob=!**/.cargo/credentials
--iglob=!.pgpass
--iglob=!.yarnrc.yml
